dossiers.title: If Found...
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players describe a hand-drawn interactive diary where the principal action is physically erasing text and images to reveal the next scene, making interaction an expressive narrative device.
This is a short and largely linear visual novel rather than a puzzle-driven adventure, with minimal player choice or systemic challenge.
An intimate story about Kasio, family rejection, acceptance and belonging strongly resonates with many readers, though others find the writing or emotional themes unengaging.
Expressive drawings, rich colors and an atmospheric soundtrack are recurring strengths that help convey the characters' feelings.
The novelty of erasing can fade and some players find the repetitive gesture tedious, while others enjoy it throughout the brief runtime.
Limited interaction and constrained pacing make it a poor match for players expecting action, branching choices or challenging puzzles.
The parallel space storyline provokes different interpretations and occasional confusion about how it relates to the personal diary plot.
The emotional pacing and short duration suit players seeking a compact reflective narrative, but leave little game-like progression outside revealing new pages.

conflicts.statement: A memorable, affecting story for some conflicts with reports that repeated erasing and the sparse mechanics feel more like passively reading a diary than playing.

dossiers.title: Call of the Sea
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 7 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Players explore a vivid island from first person, decipher environmental symbols, collect written clues and use a journal to solve mostly self-contained puzzles.
Puzzle challenge divides players: some appreciate a manageable learning curve while others find several mechanisms either overly obvious or hard to infer without searching every corner.
The adventure advances through distinct island chapters with light exploration and clue gathering, generally without combat or elaborate sandbox activities.
Walking speed, prolonged animations and searching for small triggers can interrupt momentum in a game built around traversing sizable spaces.
Many players praise the mysterious expedition, warm tropical aesthetic and expressive voice performances, finding an atmospheric contrast to darker Lovecraft-style fiction.
The emotional central story engages some players, but others describe predictable twists or a plot that feels less deep than its presentation initially promises.
The relatively brief campaign can feel fresh and focused, yet repetitive searching and similar environmental puzzle loops eventually wear thin for some.

conflicts.statement: Beautiful environments and a warmly told mystery appeal to many, while other players regard the puzzles and plot as shallow and slowed by excessive walking.

dossiers.title: Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth: Complete Edition

game_identity.work_title: Digimon Story Cyber Sleuth: Complete Edition

dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: Classic party-based turn-taking battles reward matching Digimon types, attributes and moves; collecting creatures by scanning opponents shapes the core gameplay loop.
Branching digivolution and de-digivolution allow rebuilding favorite monsters with inherited skills, creating depth at the cost of long farming and leveling sessions.
The Complete Edition combines Cyber Sleuth and Hacker's Memory stories into a substantial linked monster-collecting JRPG package.
Some boss encounters punish casual team compositions, requiring awareness of type strengths, skills and stat-building rather than relying only on preferred Digimon.
Dialogue-heavy early chapters and extended travel between small environments frustrate players who prioritize frequent battles and fast-paced monster collection.
Cyber-detective plots, character relationships and an anime-inspired visual presentation appeal to fans, though players disagree on how early the story becomes interesting.
Repetitive leveling, scanning and fetch-style errands can be substantial hurdles to completing the full package or collecting particular high-tier creatures.

Russian players reported trouble with unofficial translation files including crashes during scenes in late 2025; those complaints concern specific unofficial patches, not established defects in the unmodified edition.

conflicts.statement: Fans of the intricate monster evolution system praise its strategic experimentation, while other players consider the grind and dialogue-heavy pace excessive.
